narrativeBlocks.title: Plutarch's Theseus unites Attica
narrativeBlocks.body: Plutarch credits Theseus with bringing dispersed inhabitants into one civic community and calming disputes.

narrativeBlocks.title: The Library's Heracles receives an order
narrativeBlocks.body: The Pythian priestess directs Heracles to serve Eurystheus and perform the first ten labours.

narrativeBlocks.title: The works have different purposes
narrativeBlocks.body: Plutarch shapes a Life around civic and moral action; the Library organizes myths into genealogies and episodes.

narrativeBlocks.title: A comparison needs both passages
narrativeBlocks.body: The Theseus claim comes from Plutarch; the Heracles service comes from Pseudo-Apollodorus' Library. Neither passage defines every version of either hero.

narrativeBlocks.title: Do not turn order into a canon
narrativeBlocks.body: These selected accounts show how later authors used heroes for different narrative and political purposes.
